title: the control plane Policy Configuration record
description: Machine-validatable policy configuration (docs/spec/contracts/policy-contract.md §9). A policy holds logic; this record holds the values one deployment gives it: the parameters, the owning tenant, the scope, how strictly it is enforced, when it may run and who hears about it. It configures exactly one policy, pinned to a version (POL-012). The policy engine evaluates a configuration, never a bare policy: a policy with no active configuration decides nothing.

record_type.description: Dispatch discriminator (data-model-core §2). A policy configuration is its own record kind: the values one deployment gives a policy, kept apart from the policy's logic (POL-011).

handle.description: Advisory human identity; uuid is authoritative.

tenant_uuid.description: Owning tenant (TEN-001; data-model-core §5 [D3]). A system-domain configuration is owned by the platform tenant.

state.description: Where the configuration is in its life. `proposed` is shadow mode: the policy runs on real traffic with these values and its output is logged, never applied (POL-004). `active` applies. `deprecated` still applies, with a replacement named and a warning on evaluation. `retired` is terminal. An unpublished configuration has no status; there is no `developing` (#723).

configures.description: The one policy these values are for, as a URF reference pinned to a version or a digest (identifier-scheme §9; POL-012). The pin is required: an unpinned reference would follow the policy to its next version (URF-014), and the logic an estate runs would change with no change to any record the estate owns. Moving to a new version of the policy is a new version of this record that moves the pin.

parameters.description: The values this deployment gives the policy's parameters. The policy owns their shape: they satisfy the pinned policy's `parameter_schema`, and a policy that declares no parameters takes none (POL-013, tests/check_policy_configurations.py). UDLM does not interpret a value; the engine hands them to the rule beside the facts.

domain.description: Precedence scope of this configuration. The specific domain wins for a value: `entity` over `resource_type` over `tenant` (policy-contract §4).

enforcement.description: How strictly this deployment enforces the policy. hard = cannot be relaxed by any rule below it; soft = a default a more specific rule can tighten (policy-contract §3). The same logic can be hard in one deployment and soft in another, which is why this is not the policy's.

lifecycle_scope.description: Which lifecycle operations the policy is evaluated on in this deployment (policy-contract §2.3). A configuration of a compliance-class validation policy or a governance_matrix_rule must include 'all' at standard/prod; fsi/sovereign cannot scope out any operation.

items.description:
One temporal clause. CARRIES TIMING ONLY.

A schedule clause governs WHEN, never WHETHER (ADR-053 Decision 2). The evidence gate is the policy's `match` rule, and no schedule clause — `expedite` included — can reference it away. Expedite compresses the calendar; it never skips the diff. A policy that gated *whether* from a schedule clause would let a deadline decide a safety question, which is the failure this shape makes unrepresentable rather than merely discouraged.

kind.description: `window` — allowed execution times. `freeze` — a dated suspension that QUEUES rather than runs, so a frozen change is deferred and not lost. `expedite` — compress the calendar under elevated approval, with the audit record flagged. `precondition` — proceed only when a named predecessor stage's evidence is present (declared multi-estate chains).

recurrence.description: For a `window`: when it recurs. Inline, or sourced from a calendar the configuration names. A sourced calendar keeps one estate's holidays out of the substrate.

calendar_ref.description: A sourced calendar, as a URF reference. UDLM carries the reference; whose calendar it is, is the estate's.

predecessor_stage.description: For a `precondition`: the stage whose evidence must be present.

approval.description: A sign-off bound to the evidence it accepts — the accreditation shape, not a parallel one (ADR-053). An approval that names no digest accepts nothing in particular: the evidence can be regenerated afterwards and the signature still reads as covering it.

authority_level.description: The authority this approval was given at. An `expedite` clause requires one the configuration declares elevated. Otherwise compressing the calendar would need no more standing than following it.

accepts_digest.description: The digest of the evidence accepted — the ADR-046 promotion diff, typically. Binds the signature to bytes rather than to an intention.

reason.description: Why this clause exists. Carried for the human reading a deferral; never evaluated.

schedule.description: Temporal clauses on a configuration of a `validation` or `orchestration_flow` policy (ADR-053). When a change may run is a property of the gate as one deployment applies it: the windows, freeze dates and approvals are that deployment's. TYPED ADOPTION DEBT IS DERIVED FROM THESE, never stored: `pin_behind` (ordinary lag), `windowed` (held by a `window`), `frozen` (held by a `freeze`). A stored verdict could disagree with its clauses (DRV-001).

audit_on.description: Which decisions produce audit records (e.g. ALLOW, DENY, STRIP_FIELD).

compliance_basis.description: The regulatory citation this deployment enforces the policy under. One policy can serve two citations in two deployments.

examples.name: EU data residency — eu_personal data stays in EU zones
examples.description: One deployment's values for the data residency gate. eu_personal data may only be realized in an EU sovereignty zone. Worked example (example.com content).
